title: Portfolio risk dashboard spec for model sourcing and competitive arbitrage
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Goal: Define and deliver a product-facing dashboard that surfaces portfolio-level supply risk, competitive pricing/arbitrage signals, and procurement triggers to enable faster, evidence-backed sourcing and fallback decisions for enterprise customers. Background: Ops and sales report repeated churn risk when upstream model availability or pricing shifts suddenly. Current signals are fragmented (email, Slack, ad-hoc spreadsheets). This ticket scopes a centralized visualization and ruleset that combines availability, latency/region variance, model pricing, quantization compatibility, and contract windows into an actionable risk score and recommended next action for PMs, sales leads, and procurement.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard wireframe approved by PM and two engineering leads
Risk score computed nightly from at least five signal sources (availability, avg latency, price delta, quantization compatibility, legal/contract end-date)
Top-3 recommended actions generated per model (e.g., provision Dedicated, enable fallback to variant, engage supplier) with confidence bands
Alerting rules (email + slack) for high risk events implemented and tested on staging
End-to-end demo run with Solutions Engineering using a simulated model outage scenario
research_plan: Inventory existing signal sources: provider availability APIs, pricing feeds, infra latency dashboard, procurement contract registry
Interview GTM and Support for 6 enterprise accounts to catalog pain points and decision timelines
Prototype risk scoring heuristic (weighted signals) and validate against 6 months of historical incidents
Work with ENG to identify necessary backend indices and ingestion cadence
Design low-fidelity wireframes, run 2 design critiques, collect feedback from 5 stakeholders
early_findings: Large enterprise customers require notification windows of >=72 hours for contract-driven model changes to avoid SLA breaches
Price spikes correlate with availability drops in certain APAC regions (observed Sep-Dec 2025 dataset)
Quantization compatibility often determines feasible fallback models for memory-constrained deployments; teams lack a consolidated compatibility matrix
Current latency variance is a stronger predictor for user-visible impact than raw availability in multi-tenant Hosted deployments
next_steps: Finalize signal weighting proposal and publish to Confluence for review (owner: Liam)
ENG to provide prototype ingestion pipeline and nightly score computation (owner: Priya Rao)
Schedule design review for dashboard widgets and mobile/console variants (owner: Sara Kim)
Run two enterprise interview sessions and synthesize decision timelines into requirements (owner: Maya)
Create staging alerting rules and test with Support playbook (owner: On-call Ops)
